vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cmic-skill-scanner-linux-amd64
Version: 0.6.0

The skill bundle relies on an opaque, pre-compiled binary (assets/bin/skillscan) to perform security audits, which prevents direct inspection of its logic. It explicitly includes functionality to upload detailed scan results to external endpoints via the --upload-url flag (as seen in SKILL.md and INSTALL.md). While presented as an enterprise reporting feature, the combination of an unverified binary and built-in network exfiltration capabilities poses a significant risk for data leakage and unauthorized code execution.

llm.summary: The skill claims to be a self-contained scanner binary but the package listing does not include that binary; its runtime instructions also allow uploading full scan results to arbitrary endpoints — together these inconsistencies and exfiltration capability merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (local security scanner) matches the documented workflow, but SKILL.md explicitly claims a bundled binary at assets/bin/skillscan. The registry metadata and file manifest provided do not include that binary. Claiming a self-contained binary while shipping only docs/build metadata is an important incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent/operator to run ./assets/bin/skillscan review and documents an --upload-url option where the payload 'contains embedded review details for each skill' (i.e., full review output). That permits exfiltration of scanned package contents/metadata to arbitrary endpoints. It also documents an --engine external mode which can bridge to external scanners. Both behaviors go beyond a simple local scan and could leak sensitive content if misused.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry says this is instruction-only and no install spec is present, but SKILL.md and INSTALL.md both describe a prebuilt binary and a SHA-256 checksum. The package manifest you supplied does not list the binary file itself. This mismatch (claims of a bundled executable + checksum vs. absence of the executable) is a red flag — either the binary is missing from the published bundle or the metadata is dishonest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which is reasonable for a local scanner. However, the documented ability to upload full review contents to a user-provided URL or to bridge to external engines creates an out-of-band data flow that can leak sensitive data even without explicit credential requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced presence). The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (default), which is normal. That autonomy combined with the documented upload/bridge features increases blast radius if the binary exists and is malicious, but there is no explicit persistent/always-on behavior in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill yet. Verify whether the release actually includes assets/bin/skillscan; if it does, verify the binary's SHA-256 matches the documented checksum and obtain the source code or a trusted upstream release (preferred). Avoid using any --upload-url or external engine options until you trust the binary and the endpoint; these options will transmit full review contents (potentially sensitive) to remote servers. If you must test, run in a strongly isolated environment (air-gapped VM or sandbox) and inspect network activity. Ask the publisher for a homepage, source repository, reproducible build instructions, and a signed release; lacking those, treat the package as untrusted.
